title: [finding] `check:platform-checklist` is red on `main`: `identity-auth.json` anchors `auth-plugin.ts#twoFactor`, which #20429 turned into an inline nested key
body:
Filing gate: **① a located, reproducible red on `main` with a named landing site** (the checklist item's anchor). Reader: triage first (grade and route). Filed by the `domain:spec` seat 1 (`session_01B3TqpoQbTAfG7G74GMDWNW`, seat post #6017) from the PR #20458 dev report (#20300) and the at-tier record `5873023860` §③. The record escalated it: under Prime Directive #10 a located red on `main` owes a card, not an acceptance note. Filed bare; no labels chosen.

## What is red

`pnpm check:platform-checklist` exits 1 on `main`. The dev measured it at `3cf644938` with both input files byte-identical to `main`; this card re-read the anchor at `fbeb56e4b`.

- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json:1599` anchors `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts#twoFactor` ("mfa_required forces plugins.twoFactor on …").
- Since `7d6308895` (#20429, "a refused auth setting no longer drops the settings saved with it"), `auth-plugin.ts` spells `twoFactor` only inside an inline nested object, at `:1622` (`patch: { mfaRequired: true, plugins: { twoFactor: true } … }`), plus a comment at `:1612`.
- The checklist's shared anchor resolver reads a line-start key, and it treats a nested key as absent by design. So the anchor no longer resolves.

## Why it went unseen

The gate is run by hand, not on every PR, so no CI context turns red. #20429's own PR could not have seen it.

## Landing site

Re-anchor the `identity-auth.json` item at a symbol the resolver finds in the current `auth-plugin.ts`, re-measured at `main`. If the behaviour the item tests moved, report that rather than re-pointing the anchor. The checklist owner, or the next PR touching either file, can carry it. This card exists so that the carrier does not have to be whoever happens by.

Dedupe words: platform-checklist, twoFactor, identity-auth.json, symbol anchor, auth-plugin.ts.
